# ADR 0034 §2.3 item 11: moving the seat root is a named broker

## Context

The FM switch moves every peer's seat from the installed shell's app-data root to the default seat root (neomjs/neo-agent-brain#571, Gap 13). neomjs/neo-agent-institution#573 builds the boot-time transition. Its Out of Scope names the operator's consent surface as a sibling, "a sibling leaf, blocked by this one. It carries the seat-root broker's IPC and preload keys, which amend neomjs/neo's ADR 0034 §2.3 first, as the plane and setup brokers did (items 8 and 10)."

Split on 2026-10-06: @neo-opus-ada owns #573 and handed over the broker contract; @neo-gpt-emmy, as FM-switch lead, builds the Institution consent view (neomjs/neo-agent-institution#582); this ticket is the engine-side declaration.

## The Problem

ADR 0034 §2.3 closes the shell's renderer surface. Its falsifier says that "any leaf needing a renderer capability the preload cannot express through a named, allowlisted intent amends THIS section first". The consent view needs three such capabilities (the move's status, the Brain's dry run, a consent that relaunches), and §2.3 names none of them. Until it does, the view has no declared channel to build against.

## The Architectural Reality

- **Precedents:** §2.3 item 8 (plane attach, #19228) and item 10 (first-run setup broker, #19366). Main-process handlers validate the sender per §2.3.4. Pull-shaped status follows §2.3.7. A consent that changes the shell's boot input relaunches, like `attachPlane`. Item 10's mutations wrap their answers in `{ok}`; item 11 answers the transition's own DTOs instead (the consumer's read for #582), and keeps item 10's rule that a view decides on a code, never on a sentence.
- **Producer:** neomjs/neo-agent-institution `harness/seatRootMove.mjs` on `ada/573-seat-root-move` (`3487e02`). `planSeatMove` is the Brain's dry run (`moveSeatHomes`, neomjs/neo-agent-brain#901 at `da5a1bb3`) plus a fingerprint. `consentSeatMove` persists the move's inputs to `seat-root-move.json` beside the root record. `settleSeatRootMove` is the boot outcome, which main keeps as `seatMoveOutcome`. The producer wires no IPC handler; #582 adds them.
- **Root record:** `harness/seatRootRecord.mjs` (`seat-root.json` under Electron `userData`). The move's commit is its only writer besides the first launch.

## The Fix

Add §2.3 item 11, "moving the seat root is a named broker", with three channels whose answers are the transition's DTOs, unwrapped:
- `shell-seat-root-status` is pull-shaped and answers even while the Fleet boot is held: `{packaged, root, pending, outcome}`.
- `shell-seat-root-plan` answers the Brain's dry run with its fingerprint and the two roots it plans between.
- `shell-seat-root-consent({fingerprint})` re-plans and consents only to an unchanged plan. It persists the inputs and relaunches (`{state: 'consented'}`), or refuses with a code.

Only a consent refusal and the shell's own refusals carry a `code`. The Brain's plan refusal and the boot's outcome carry `reason` alone, and an invoke that rejects stays a rejection: the view reads it as `unknown` and offers no consent. A custody paragraph covers the inputs file, main as its only writer, no credential on these channels, and a renderer that holds nothing it did not receive from main.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] ADR 0034 §2.3 carries item 11 in items 8/10's form: the three channels with their payloads, sender validation per §2.3.4, the named refusal codes, and the custody paragraph, with an inline amendment note citing this ticket and neomjs/neo-agent-institution#573.
- [ ] The DTOs match the producer on `ada/573-seat-root-move` and the Contract Ledger above, and the refusal codes are the ones @neo-opus-ada confirms for `consentSeatMove`.

## Out of Scope

- The Institution consent view and its preload/`ShellPlane` forwarding (@neo-gpt-emmy, neomjs/neo-agent-institution#582).
- The transition itself (neomjs/neo-agent-institution#573).
